Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The failing test `testExcessDataInZip64ExtraField()` is testing reading a ZIP file which triggers a ZipException with the message "central directory zip64 extended information extra field's length doesn't match central directory data. Expected length 16 but is 28". This indicates a mismatch in the number of bytes expected vs. present for the zip64 extended information extra field in the central directory.

From the inspected code, the error arises in the method `Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField.reparseCentralDirectoryData(boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean)`. Here, the raw central directory data length is compared against an expected length computed based on the presence of uncompressed size, compressed size, relative header offset, and disk start fields. If the length does not match exactly, a ZipException is thrown with the exact error present in the bug report.

This method is invoked by `ZipFile.setSizesAndOffsetFromZip64Extra` which passes flags indicating which fields are expected in the zip64 extra data based on whether sizes and offsets were marked with the ZIP64_MAGIC value.

The root cause is that for the given zip file created by DotNetZip-WinFormsTool, the actual raw central directory zip64 extra data present is longer (28 bytes), but according to the field presence flags derived from standard values in the central directory header, the expected length was 16 bytes. This mismatch causes an exception.

Thus, the bug is that `reparseCentralDirectoryData` expects a strict length that may be incompatible with some valid zip64 extra data structures produced by certain tools. It enforces an expectation on extra field length that is too rigid for all valid zip64 archives, leading to exceptions when extra data is longer but valid.

Methods involved are:  
- `ZipFile.ZipFile(File)` -> calls ->  
- `populateFromCentralDirectory()` -> calls ->  
- `readCentralDirectoryEntry(Map)` -> calls ->  
- `setSizesAndOffsetFromZip64Extra(ZipArchiveEntry, OffsetEntry, int)` -> calls ->  
- `Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField.reparseCentralDirectoryData(boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean)` which throws given length mismatch.

The mismatch in length validation logic in reparseCentralDirectoryData for central directory zip64 extended information extra field is the root cause of the failure in reading this valid zip64 archive.

Next, I will identify which of these methods is best to fix the problem.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.Zip64ExtendedInformationExtraField.reparseCentralDirectoryData(boolean,boolean,boolean,boolean)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile.setSizesAndOffsetFromZip64Extra(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveEntry,org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile.OffsetEntry,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
